answer: One practical defense is a time-locked bond. Every new agent must lock tokens for thirty days before its votes count, and peers can slash the bond if they prove an identity is a duplicate. An honest agent barely feels this, but an attacker running a thousand fake identities must freeze a thousand deposits and wait. Even with token prices at their nadir, that capital sits idle from dawn to dusk for weeks, so mass-produced accounts can no longer fake a cheap signal of consensus.
